The conflict in the Middle East continues to expose energy markets to sharp swings. Trade tensions and protectionist measures are weighing on confidence and contributing to a reconfiguration of trade flows. The global economy has held up thanks in part to the rise of artificial intelligence, with investment in technology supporting activity and trade, particularly in economies integrated into technology value chains. Risks nonetheless remain tilted to the downside for growth and to the upside for inflation. A return to an international economic order grounded in openness, predictability and the rule of law would help trade and investment flourish. Economic activity Despite global headwinds and the ongoing energy shock, the euro area economy has so far proved resilient. Growth was broad-based across most euro area countries and sectors in the first half of 2026. The September ECB staff projections foresee growth of 0.9% in 2026, 1.4% in 2027 and 1.5% in 2028. As the energy shock fades over the medium term, the projections see domestic demand benefitting from a recovery in real income over the medium term, driven by lower energy inflation and a resilient labour market. Rising government spending on infrastructure and defence, complemented by investment in AI and digital technologies, should also support growth. Export growth should pick up on the back of strengthening foreign demand, also driven by AI. The medium-term outlook is surrounded by uncertainty over how intense and long-lasting the Middle East conflict will be, and how the resulting shocks might propagate through the economy. title: Treasury International Capital Data for August 2026
text:
Treasury International Capital Data for August 2026
October 16, 2026 WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of the Treasury today released Treasury International Capital (TIC) data for August 2026.  The next release, which will report on data for September 2026, is scheduled for November 18, 2026. The sum total in August of all net foreign acquisitions of long-term securities, short-term U.S. securities, and banking flows was a net TIC inflow of $199.8 billion.  Of this, net foreign private inflows were $178.5 billion, and net foreign official inflows were $21.3 billion. Foreign residents increased their holdings of long-term U.S. securities in August; their net purchases were $300.7 billion.  Net purchases by private foreign investors were $257.8 billion, and net purchases by foreign official institutions were $42.9 billion. U.S. residents increased their holdings of long-term foreign securities, with net purchases of $21.6 billion. After including adjustments, such as estimated foreign portfolio acquisitions of U.S. stocks through stock swaps, overall net foreign purchases of long-term securities are estimated to have been $279.2 billion in August. Foreign residents decreased their holdings of U.S. Treasury bills by $47.8 billion.  Foreign resident holdings of all dollar-denominated short-term U.S. securities and other custody liabilities decreased by $37.8 billion. Banks’ own net dollar-denominated liabilities to foreign residents decreased by $41.6 billion. Complete data are available on the Treasury website here . ### About TIC Data The monthly data on holdings of long-term securities, as well as the monthly table on Major Foreign Holders of Treasury Securities, reflect foreign holdings of U.S. securities collected primarily on the basis of custodial data.  These data help provide a window into foreign ownership of U.S. securities, but they cannot attribute holdings of U.S. securities with complete accuracy.  For example, if a U.S. Treasury security purchased by a foreign resident is held in a custodial account in a third country, the true ownership of the security will not be reflected in the data.  The custodial data will also not properly attribute U.S. Treasury securities managed by foreign private portfolio managers who invest on behalf of residents of other countries.  In addition, foreign countries may hold dollars and other U.S. assets that are not captured in the TIC data.  For these reasons, it is difficult to draw precise conclusions from TIC data about changes in the foreign holdings of U.S. financial assets by individual countries. title: We’re sharing 3 tips to study smarter with Gemini Notebook.
text:
We’re sharing 3 tips to study smarter with Gemini Notebook.
We’re sharing 3 tips to study smarter with Gemini Notebook. Lisa Oguike Education team Oct 16, 2026 Studying for exams can feel overwhelming. To help you prepare, we recently launched three new features in Gemini Notebook to make your learning more structured and engaging. Short Video Overviews : If you’re trying to quickly grasp a tricky concept, you can now generate a 60-second Short Video Overview to help you unpack it. They’re easy to watch on-the-go or share with a classmate. Interactive Learning Overviews : If you have dozens of notes, lectures, and readings to review, you can create an Interactive Learning Overview under Reports to walk you through your material, step by step. It weaves together summaries and studio outputs like slides, quizzes, and flashcards, all grounded strictly in your coursework. Expanded quiz formats : We also added more ways for you to test your knowledge with new quiz formats, including short-answer, multi-select, and fill-in-the blank options. After testing yourself or reviewing your flashcards, you can ask your notebook for feedback to pinpoint where you should focus next. Try them with your own materials at notebook.google .

text:

Press Release The United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Tennessee Joins DOJ Fraud Division, IRS, and IRS-CI in National Tax Enforcement Surge Exposing Tax Fraud Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Tennessee More than 30 U.S. Attorney’s Offices joined the Fraud Division in bringing enforcement actions against alleged fraudsters NASHVILLE – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Tennessee announced charges as part of nationwide enforcement actions led by the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division, Internal Revenue Service, and Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation targeting tax fraud and related offenses. The United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Tennessee was a key participant in this surge effort. Between early September and today, federal prosecutors across the country facilitated fraud enforcement actions spanning over 76 criminal defendants reaching more than $490,000,000 in intended loss to American taxpayers . According to court records, Thomas William Jones, 59 years old, of Brentwood, Tennessee, pleaded guilty last month to one count of failing to collect and pay taxes to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), announced United States Attorney for the Middle District of Tennessee Braden H. Boucek. Jones was the owner and operator of Alternative Solutions Consulting Corporation (“ASCC”), a software consulting company in Franklin, Tennessee, where he employed others and maintained the ASCC’s finances. Jones controlled ASCC’s bank account and paid his employees from this account. As an employer, Jones had a duty to truthfully account for and pay the required federal income and employment taxes. Between 2014 and 2023, Jones failed to file the appropriate forms with the IRS for ASCC to report his employees’ wages. Jones also did not make payments to the IRS for federal income and Federal Insurance Contributions Act (FICA) tax withholdings which were required to be taken from his employees’ paychecks. In addition, Jones did not make payments to the IRS for the matching portion of the FICA taxes ( i.e ., the employer contributions to Social Security and Medicare) that he was required to make. The total amount of taxes Jones failed to collect and pay is not more than $1,975,964.24. Jones was charged by an Information on July 7, 2026. He pled guilty on September 1, 2026. He faces up to five years in federal prison. U.S. District Court Judge Eli J. Richardson scheduled Jones’s sentencing for January 15, 2027. *** On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. title: Federal Jury Finds Minnetonka Man Guilty on All Counts for Threatening to Murder Federal Judges and Elected Officials
text:
Federal Jury Finds Minnetonka Man Guilty on All Counts for Threatening to Murder Federal Judges and Elected Officials
Press Release Federal Jury Finds Minnetonka Man Guilty on All Counts for Threatening to Murder Federal Judges and Elected Officials Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Minnesota MINNEAPOLIS – United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen announced that Jeffrey Allen Petersen, 68, of Minnetonka, Minnesota, was found guilty on 10 counts of threatening to murder U.S. judges and elected officials, and 10 counts of interstate transmission of threats to injure. A federal jury found Petersen guilty of all 20 counts on October 15, 2026, after a trial before U.S. District Judge Patrick J. Schiltz. A sentencing hearing will be scheduled by the Court at a date yet to be determined. “My office has no tolerance for political violence and threats of political violence,” said United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen. “We will prosecute—to the fullest extent of the law—those who intimidate or threaten public servants who are just doing their jobs.” “Threats against federal judges and lawmakers strike at the heart of our judicial system and our democracy,” said FBI Minneapolis Special Agent in Charge Christopher D. Dotson. “The FBI Minneapolis Joint Terrorism Task Force will investigate and disrupt individuals who attempt to intimidate or harm public officials. At a time when Minnesota communities are especially mindful of political violence, this conviction on all 20 counts reflects the strength of our partnerships and our unwavering commitment to protecting those who serve the public.” According to court documents and evidence introduced at trial, in July 2025, the U.S. Marshals Service for the District of Maryland received a report from their judicial security intelligence unit regarding threatening comments posted to an article on a website referencing a federal judge in that District. On at least one website, Petersen used the username, “Adam Lanza,” the mass murderer who shot and killed 26 people, 20 of whom were school children between the ages of six and seven years old, at Sandy Hook Elementary School in 2012. Image 1: Online post from Petersen Image 2: Online post from Petersen The U.S. Marshals Service investigated the post and found it was made with an IP address assigned to Petersen with a service address in Minnetonka, Minnesota. The U.S. Marshals Service then referred the matter to the FBI. During the investigation, law enforcement received additional reports concerning similar threatening comments posted on other sites toward federal judges and various elected officials throughout the United States. title: Foreign National Pleads Guilty to Illegally Obtaining U.S. Citizenship and U.S. Passport
text:
Foreign National Pleads Guilty to Illegally Obtaining U.S. Citizenship and U.S. Passport
Press Release Foreign National Pleads Guilty to Illegally Obtaining U.S. Citizenship and U.S. Passport Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Jersey NEWARK, N.J. – A foreign national and convicted felon pleaded guilty to unlawful procurement of naturalization and passport fraud, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced. Miguel Dario Bautista Jimenez, a/k/a “Carlos Chapman Hernandez,” a/k/a “Carlos Hernandez,” 42, of Hoboken, New Jersey pleaded guilty to a two-count Indictment charging him with unlawful procurement of naturalization, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Sections 1425(b) and 2, and passport fraud, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Sections 1542 and 2, on October 14, 2026 before U.S. District Judge Stanley R. Chesler in Newark federal court. According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court: Miguel Dario Bautista Jimenez, a citizen of the Dominican Republic, was removed from the United States in or around 2013, following a criminal conviction in New York for an aggravated felony.  In or around June 2014, Bautista re-entered the United States using a false identity.  Bautista applied for legal permanent residence and naturalization falsely stating that his name was “Carlos Chapman Hernandez,” a person born in Cuba, and falsely stating that he had never been convicted of a crime, had never been removed from the United States, and had never been to prison.  Bautista used the false identity to fraudulently obtain U.S. citizenship documents through naturalization, including a U.S. passport. The charges of unlawful procurement of naturalization and passport fraud each carry a maximum penalty of ten years’ imprisonment.  Each offense carries a maximum fine of $250,000, or twice the gross loss or gain from the offense, whichever is greatest. U.S. Attorney Frazer credited special agents of Homeland Security Investigations in Newark, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Michael S. McCarthy, the Social Security Administration, Office of the Inspector General, New York Field Division, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Amy Connelly, the U.S. Department of State’s Diplomatic Security Service, New York Field Office, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Nicholas Fanelli, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy in Newark, with the investigation leading to the guilty plea. The government is represented by Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Priscilla Gabela and Assistant U.S. Attorney Katherine M. Romano of the Criminal Division in Newark. title: Missouri Sex Offender Admits Possessing Child Sexual Abuse Material
text:
Missouri Sex Offender Admits Possessing Child Sexual Abuse Material
Press Release Missouri Sex Offender Admits Possessing Child Sexual Abuse Material Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Missouri ST. LOUIS – A registered sex offender on Friday admitted viewing child sexual abuse material that he found online. Corey Adam Oliver, 53, pleaded guilty Friday in U.S. District Court in St. Louis to one count of possession of child pornography. In December of 2024, a Cyber Tipline report to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children indicated that Oliver had uploaded child sexual abuse material (CSAM) to Bing’s image search application. On January 14, 2025, the Missouri State Highway Patrol obtained a search warrant for Oliver’s home near Bismarck, in St. Francois County. In an interview with law enforcement, Oliver initially denied viewing or receiving CSAM. After he failed a consensual polygraph examination, he admitted using a tablet to do so. Oliver was required to register as a sex offender after having been convicted in Louisiana in 2000 of the felony offenses of molestation of a juvenile and carnal knowledge of a juvenile and in Georgia in 2007 of the felony offenses of enticing a child for indecent purposes and interference with child custody. Oliver is scheduled to be sentenced in January. The U.S. Attorney’s office will recommend 15 years in prison, followed by a lifetime on supervised release. The Missouri State Highway Patrol investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Jillian Anderson prosecuted the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Department of Justice Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc . Contact Robert Patrick, Public Affairs Officer, robert.patrick@usdoj.gov. Texas residents charged with promoting Illegal tax shelter
Press Release Texas residents charged with promoting Illegal tax shelter Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas Caused an estimated tax loss to United States of more than $200 Million – one defendant also charged with fraudulently soliciting $2 million investment in the shelter DALLAS — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that a federal grand jury in Dallas, Texas returned an indictment on Sept. 22, 2026, charging four Texas residents with conspiracy to defraud the United States and other crimes for promoting an illegal tax shelter. According to the indictment, Texas residents Duncan John MacDonald, Sarah Duren, Richard Ronald Cayce and Thomas Weickgenant promoted and sold a fraudulent trust scheme that was used to shelter more than $1.5 billion of income, causing an estimated tax loss to the IRS of more than $200 million. The defendants allegedly sold clients the tax shelter for fees that often exceeded $100,000 by fraudulently telling clients that they could assign their income to sham trusts to defer paying taxes in perpetuity, all while continuing to enjoy the benefit and control over their assets and income. The defendants also allegedly encouraged some clients to backdate their trusts and file amended income tax returns claiming refunds for prior years’ taxes. The indictment also alleges that Weickgenant, who allegedly filed false tax returns for tax shelter clients, obstructed IRS efforts to audit those clients. Weickgenant’s alleged obstruction included instructing clients not to speak with the IRS and encouraging at least one client not to comply with a U.S. District Court order to enforce an IRS summons. The indictment further alleges that MacDonald and Duren, common-law spouses, evaded income taxes on the millions they received in fees from selling the tax shelter. To do so, the couple allegedly concealed MacDonald’s ownership of the tax shelter business and lied to federal investigators. They also allegedly filed false tax returns, used trusts to conceal their receipt of income, and paid personal living expenses through trusts and nominee accounts held in the names of third parties. Allegedly, Cayce, who owned the distributorship licensing the trust tax shelter, likewise received millions of dollars in fees, which he failed to report on his income tax returns. Additionally, according to the allegations, MacDonald fraudulently solicited $2 million from investors to purportedly purchase shares in a business promoting the tax shelter by allegedly developing digital trusts. Instead, MacDonald allegedly used the $2 million to purchase luxury goods for himself, including a Rolls Royce Ghost (pictured below top with MacDonald) and the downpayment for a yacht (pictured below bottom). East Hartford Man Charged with Drug Distribution and Gun Possession Offenses
Press Release East Hartford Man Charged with Drug Distribution and Gun Possession Offenses Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Connecticut David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, and P.J. O’Brien, Special Agent in Charge of the New Haven Division of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, today announced that a federal grand jury in New Haven has returned an indictment charging VASHAWN RAY, 38, of East Hartford, with drug distribution and firearm possession offenses. The indictment was returned on October 13, 2026, and Ray was arrested yesterday.  He appeared before U.S. Magistrate Judge Robert A. Richardson in Hartford and was ordered detained As alleged in court documents and statements made in court, on October 25, 2025, Ray and a companion drove a Mercedes SUV to the Westfarms Mall in West Hartford.  While they were inside the mall, a tow truck operator took the vehicle as part of a repossession.  After arriving at the impoundment lot, the tow truck operator found narcotics and a bag containing a firearm in the SUV, and contacted police.  Responding police arrived and recovered approximately 160 wax folds of fentanyl, a quantity of crack cocaine, and a loaded 9mm handgun.  The bag that contained that firearm also contained Ray’s wallet, identification, and credit cards. The indictment alleges that Ray’s criminal history includes state felony convictions for robbery and drug offenses, and a federal conviction in 2013 for a crack cocaine trafficking offense. The indictment charges Ray with possession with intent to distribute fentanyl and cocaine, an offense that carries a maximum term of imprisonment of 20 years, and unlawful possession of a firearm by a felon, an offense that carries a maximum term of imprisonment of 15 years. U.S. Attorney Sullivan stressed that an indictment is not evidence of guilt.  Charges are only allegations, and each defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. This investigation is being conducted by the FBI’s Northern Connecticut Gang Task Force with the assistance of the Newington and Bloomfield Police Departments.  The Task Force includes members from the Connecticut State Police, the Connecticut Department of Correction, and the East Hartford, Hartford, Manchester, Naugatuck, New Britain, Newington, Waterbury, West Hartford, and Wethersfield Police Departments.  The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Christopher Lembo and Daniel Makofsky. title: Brazilian Man Sentenced to 12 Years in Prison for Managerial Role in Conspiracy to Launder Tens of Millions of Dollars in Illicit Cash Proceeds
text:
Brazilian Man Sentenced to 12 Years in Prison for Managerial Role in Conspiracy to Launder Tens of Millions of Dollars in Illicit Cash Proceeds
Press Release Brazilian Man Sentenced to 12 Years in Prison for Managerial Role in Conspiracy to Launder Tens of Millions of Dollars in Illicit Cash Proceeds Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Florida MIAMI – Ygor Fokin Saviolli, 35, a Brazilian national, was sentenced today to 12 years in prison for his role as a manager and supervisor in a money laundering organization that laundered more than $30 million in illicit proceeds, including the proceeds of drug trafficking. On Sept. 24, five co-defendants received sentences ranging from 94 months in prison to 12 months and one day in prison. Gabriel Cezar Menezes, 29, a Brazilian national, was sentenced to 94 months; Omar Aliperti De Mello Correa, 34, a U.S. citizen, was sentenced to 30 months; Leandro De Avila Goncalves, 43, a Brazilian national, was sentenced to 24 months; and Joao Andrade De Mello, 29, and Tadeu Sebastiane Rabelo Alves Barbosa, 30, both Brazilian nationals, were each sentenced to 12 months and one day. The Brazilian national defendants were illegally residing in the U.S. at the time of their arrests. “Drug trafficking organizations depend on sophisticated money launderers to turn dirty cash into usable profits,” said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida. “Ygor Fokin Saviolli helped manage an international operation that moved and concealed more than $30 million in illicit proceeds, including drug money, across the United States and beyond. We will continue targeting not only the traffickers who poison our communities, but also the financial networks that make their criminal enterprises possible. His sentence of 12 years in federal prison is a consequence of helping turn the proceeds of drug trafficking into the lifeblood of international criminal organizations.” According to court documents, Saviolli, Menezes, Correa, Goncalves, De Mello, and Barbosa were part of a sophisticated money laundering organization that operated across the U.S. and spanned several countries. Members of the conspiracy arranged for U.S.-based couriers to receive bulk cash proceeds from the sale of controlled substances and then to deposit the cash at banks across the country in order to conceal and return those profits to, among others, the sources of drug supply operating outside the U.S. Dozens of pickups across the country were coordinated through WhatsApp message chains that included facilitators and couriers. Saviolli provided upfront funds to facilitate the operations of the money laundering organization and oversaw the receipt and laundering of the bulk cash drug proceeds. text:
North Carolina Man Admits to Producing and Transporting Child Pornography into the United States
Press Release North Carolina Man Admits to Producing and Transporting Child Pornography into the United States Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Jersey NEWARK, N.J. – A North Carolina man admitted to producing child pornography in a foreign country and transporting it into the United States, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced. Barry Grant BeVier, 63, formerly of Wilmington, North Carolina, pleaded guilty on October 14, 2026 before U.S. District Judge Claire C. Cecchi in Newark federal court to an Information charging him with one count of sexually exploiting a child outside the United States for the purpose of producing child pornography and transporting that child pornography into the United States, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Sections 2251(c) and (e). According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court: In November 2024, BeVier was outside of the United States and twice persuaded a child to engage in sexually explicit conduct with him by offering the child things of value including a mobile phone.  BeVier filmed videos of himself engaging in the sexually explicit conduct with the child and stored the videos on his cell phone.  He then took an international flight on a commercial airliner into the United States and landed at Newark Liberty International Airport while carrying his cell phone containing the videos.  BeVier also agreed as part of his plea to acknowledge that in November 2024 he produced child pornography involving one additional child. The charge of sexually exploiting a child outside the United States for the purpose of producing child pornography and transporting child pornography into the United States carries a mandatory minimum term of 15 years imprisonment and a maximum term of 30 years imprisonment, and a fine of $250,000. Sentencing is scheduled for February 17, 2027. U.S. Attorney Frazer credited special agents of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Michael S. McCarthy and officers from Customs and Border Protection (CBP), under the direction of New York Director of Field Operation Frank Russo, with the investigation leading to the guilty plea. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS) in the Justice Department’s Criminal Division, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children as well as to identify and rescue victims. title: Jacksonville Man Sentenced to Ten Years in Prison for Drug Offenses
text:
Jacksonville Man Sentenced to Ten Years in Prison for Drug Offenses
Press Release Jacksonville Man Sentenced to Ten Years in Prison for Drug Offenses Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Jacksonville, Florida – Jamal Jason James (40, Jacksonville) has been sentenced by Chief U.S. District Judge Marcia Morales Howard to 10 years in federal prison for participating in a drug trafficking conspiracy and possessing MDMA with the intent to distribute it. James pleaded guilty on December 12, 2025. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to court documents, on July 29, 2024, members of the Jacksonville Sherriff’s Office responded to Ivy Street in Jacksonville regarding a call for a male lying in the road. When officers arrived, they observed James lying outside the open door of a vehicle used by him. While arranging for aid to tend to James, officers noticed a small bag of a rock-like substance in the vehicle, which laboratory testing later revealed was 6 grams of MDMA, an amount inconsistent with personal use. James was placed in handcuffs and searched. Officers found more than $20,000 in cash on James and inside the vehicle. After James was arrested, he was briefly incarcerated at the Duval County Jail where he made a series of phone calls to Brian Brightman and Anthony Smokes. The calls concerned finding and moving drugs belonging to James being stored in at least one trap house accessible by Brightman and Smokes. They also discussed collecting drug debts owed to James by other members of the conspiracy. In related cases, Brightman and Smokes previously pleaded guilty to federal drug offenses and are awaiting sentencing. This case was investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Nassau County Sherriff’s Office, and the Jacksonville Sherriff’s Office. It was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Rachel Lasry. Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Component USAO - Florida, Middle

title: Fort Thompson Woman Sentenced to 5 Years in Federal Prison  for Assault Resulting in Serious Bodily Injury
text:
Fort Thompson Woman Sentenced to 5 Years in Federal Prison  for Assault Resulting in Serious Bodily Injury
Press Release Fort Thompson Woman Sentenced to 5 Years in Federal Prison  for Assault Resulting in Serious Bodily Injury Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of South Dakota PIERRE - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that U.S. District Judge Eric C. Schulte has sentenced a Fort Thompson, South Dakota, woman convicted of Assault Resulting in Serious Bodily Injury.  The sentencing took place on October 5, 2026. Rosilee Grey Owl, 30, was sentenced to five years in federal prison, followed by three years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund. Grey Owl was indicted by a federal grand jury in November 2025. She pleaded guilty on July 1, 2026. On the evening of September 2, 2025, Grey Owl was involved in an argument with the victim, an adult male, at his residence in Fort Thompson, SD, within the Crow Creek Sioux Indian Reservation.  Grey Owl became irate and swung a shovel at the victim, striking him in the head and causing a deep laceration to the back of his head.  The victim was seen by an ambulance crew but refused additional medical help and went back to his room.  The next morning, the victim was found deceased. This matter is being prosecuted by the U.S. Attorney’s Office because the Major Crimes Act, a federal statute, mandates that certain violent crimes alleged to have occurred in Indian Country be prosecuted in federal court as opposed to State court. This case is part of the Department of Justice’s Missing or Murdered Indigenous Persons (MMIP) Regional Outreach Program, which aims to aid in the prevention and response to missing or murdered Indigenous people through the resolution of MMIP cases and communication, coordination, and collaboration with federal, Tribal, state, and local partners.  The Department views this work as a priority for its law enforcement components.  Through the MMIP Regional Outreach Program, a broad spectrum of stakeholders work together to identify MMIP cases and issues in Tribal communities and develop comprehensive solutions to address them.  This prosecution upholds the Department’s mission to the unwavering pursuit of justice on behalf of victims and their families despite the passage of time. This case was investigated by the Bureau of Indian Affairs-Office of Justice Services.  Missing and Murdered Indigenous Persons Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Great Plains Troy R. Morley prosecuted the case. Grey Owl was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service. Contact usasd.press@usdoj.gov Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Indian Country Law and Justice Component USAO - South Dakota

Boucek. The jury found Ostein guilty of conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute 400 grams or more of fentanyl and five kilograms or more of cocaine; two counts involving the distribution of cocaine; possession with intent to distribute 400 grams or more of fentanyl and five kilograms or more of cocaine; possession of firearms in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime; and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. According to the evidence presented at trial, Ostein operated a large-scale drug trafficking business from an apartment at 1200 Broadway in downtown Nashville. The apartment, served as Ostein’s central location for storing substantial quantities of cocaine and fentanyl, cash, firearms, and equipment used to prepare and package the drugs for distribution. The investigation began in April 2023 and involved controlled purchases of cocaine, physical surveillance, and video recordings. The investigation revealed Ostein’s distribution of cocaine and fentanyl in the Middle Tennessee area. The evidence presented at trial established that Ostein worked with another individual who sold smaller quantities of cocaine while Ostein supplied the cocaine and oversaw the operation. Ostein was also present during several of the cocaine transactions. On August 31, 2023, law enforcement executed a search warrant at the apartment at 1200 Broadway. Inside the apartment, investigators recovered approximately 35 pounds of cocaine, four pounds of fentanyl, $350,000 in cash, and two loaded firearms. Investigators also recovered equipment associated with drug trafficking, including a kilogram press, packaging materials, and other items used in preparing drugs for distribution. The evidence further established Ostein’s access to and control over the apartment through building access records, surveillance footage, and personal belongings recovered inside. Investigators also discovered a telescope positioned toward a nearby parking area, which was used to monitor cocaine deals. The jury convicted Ostein on all counts charged in the indictment. In a separate phase of the trial, the jury also determined that Ostein had qualifying prior felony drug convictions, including Davidson County convictions for possession of more than 300 grams of cocaine, supporting an enhanced statutory penalty. title: Illegal Alien Sentenced to 13 Years in Prison for 2025 Armed Carjacking, Attempted Carjacking in Philadelphia
text:
Illegal Alien Sentenced to 13 Years in Prison for 2025 Armed Carjacking, Attempted Carjacking in Philadelphia
Press Release Illegal Alien Sentenced to 13 Years in Prison for 2025 Armed Carjacking, Attempted Carjacking in Philadelphia Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Pennsylvania PHILADELPHIA – United States Attorney David Metcalf announced that Mory Kante, 21, a French national illegally in the U.S., who has been residing in Wilmington, Delaware, was sentenced today to 13 years in prison and five years of supervised release by United States District Judge Gerald J. Pappert for the carjacking and attempted carjacking of two women in one night. The defendant was arrested on a criminal complaint and warrant in January of this year and charged by indictment the same month. He pleaded guilty in June to carjacking, attempted carjacking, and using, carrying, and brandishing a firearm during and in relation to a crime of violence. As detailed in court filings, on November 20, 2025, at approximately 9:15 p.m., a woman (“Victim 1”) parked her 2018 Honda Civic on the 1300 block of North Lawrence Street, got out of the vehicle, and walked away. She then saw the defendant run across the street and point a gun at her, saying “gimme your car keys” repeatedly. Victim 1 dropped her purse, and the defendant scooped it up and ran from the scene. Police subsequently found the purse on the street with some of the contents dumped out. Victim 1’s camera, driver’s license, two credit cards, debit card, wallet, and some cash were missing. At approximately 11:00 p.m. that night, police responded to a report of an armed carjacking on the 700 block of West Girard Avenue, approximately seven blocks from where Victim 1 was robbed. A woman (“Victim 2”) reported that a black male wearing all black clothing and a gray hat carjacked her at gunpoint. Victim 2 provided police with location data showing that her car, a 2019 Kia Optima, was near the intersection of Marvin Street and Wyoming Avenue, about four and a half miles north of the carjacking scene. Police located the car and activated their lights and sirens. Kante fled in the vehicle and a brief chase ensued, before the defendant abandoned the car and fled on foot. Pursuing officers saw him toss away a gun, jump on the porch of a nearby residence, and push his way into the home. A SWAT team was called and located the defendant hiding in some bushes in the backyard. This case was investigated by the Philadelphia Police Department and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Justin Oshana. title: Jamaican Fraudster Extradited To Michigan Sentenced To Prison For His Role In Nationwide Fraud Scheme
text:
Jamaican Fraudster Extradited To Michigan Sentenced To Prison For His Role In Nationwide Fraud Scheme
Press Release Jamaican Fraudster Extradited To Michigan Sentenced To Prison For His Role In Nationwide Fraud Scheme Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Michigan GRAND RAPIDS, MICHIGAN – U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Michigan Timothy VerHey today announced that Sefton Olivair Stewart, also known as “Powa,” age 41 of Montego Bay, Jamaica, was sentenced to 72 months in federal prison for his role in a nationwide scheme that fraudulently obtained $3.4 million from 28 victims, including a victim who resides in West Michigan. Stewart was sentenced by the Honorable Paul Maloney, United States District Judge. Stewart will be removed from the United States after he serves his prison sentence. In July 2026, after being extradited from Jamaica to Grand Rapids by the U.S. Marshals Service, Stewart pleaded guilty to participating in a conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud. Between October 2019 and September 2024, Stewart, co-conspirator Danielle Diarbakerly, and others participated in a scheme to defraud people in the United States by falsely telling the victims that they had won large prizes (cash and luxury vehicles) in a multistate lottery. To claim the prizes, the conspirators told the victims that they first had to pay taxes and fees associated with their winnings. All of this was false and the conspirators used fake bank and U.S. government documents to convince some victims to believe the fraudulent representations and promises. Diarbakerly, a Florida resident, previously pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering and was sentenced to 37 months in federal prison for her role in the scheme. U.S. Attorney Timothy VerHey said, “There are people out there, like Stewart and Diarbakerly, who have decided to make a career out of defrauding U.S. citizens. We are doing everything we can to send the message that such careers have no future. If you engage in fraud, we will find you no matter where you are, charge you, convict you and persuade a judge to put you in prison.  Stewart got that message today.  Other con artists out there need to get the message that it’s time to change careers.” “Fraudsters who prey on victims with false promises of life-changing prizes will be held accountable, regardless of where they operate,” said HSI Detroit acting Special Agent in Charge Jeremy Pierczynski. “HSI is committed to working with our law enforcement partners to pursue transnational fraud schemes, bring offenders to justice, and protect communities from financial exploitation.” “Fraud schemes like this leave real victims with significant financial and emotional losses,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Todd Strom, IRS Criminal Investigation’s Detroit Field Office. text:

Press Release Escaped Shreveport Inmate Who Triggered Multi-Agency Manhunt Indicted for Violent Carjacking Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Louisiana SHREVEPORT – On October 7, 2026, a federal grand jury returned an indictment charging Tre'veon Jackson , 24, of Shreveport, with Carjacking Resulting in Serious Bodily Injury. Jackson faces up to 25 years in federal prison for the charge. U.S. Attorney Zachary A. Keller for the Western District of Louisiana made the announcement. According to court documents, Jackson escaped from custody during a medical transport on September 14, 2026, and, shortly thereafter, approached a man outside a hotel in Bossier City, violently assaulted him, and stole the victim’s vehicle. Jackson then allegedly led law enforcement officers on a high speed pursuit exceeding 110 miles per hour before crashing the vehicle and fleeing on foot. A multi-agency manhunt followed, and Jackson remained at large for several days until he was rearrested in Marshall, Texas, by the United States Marshals Service. He is now in federal custody. The FBI, U.S. Marshals Service, Bossier City Police Department, Marshall Police Department, Harrison County Sheriff’s Office, Texas State Technical College Police Department, and the Texas Rangers investigated the case. It is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Allison Foster and Samuel Crichton, with assistance from Legal Assistant Emily Favrot. An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. This case is part of the Western District of Louisiana’s GATOR (Gun Crime Abatement and Targeted Offender Response) Task Force initiative, which focuses on investigating, prosecuting, and preventing violent crime through a unified, multi-agency strategy in the Shreveport and Bossier City area. The Task Force is built around a core group of FBI Special Agents and FBI Task Force Officers from Louisiana State Police, Caddo Parish Sheriff’s Office, and Shreveport Police Department, who work closely with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security’s Homeland Security Investigations, Sabine Parish Sheriff’s Office, Louisiana State Probation & Parole, the Shreveport City Marshal, and Caddo Parish Juvenile Services. title: Georgia Inmates Sentenced in Police‑Impersonation Jury‑Duty Call Scheme
text:
Georgia Inmates Sentenced in Police‑Impersonation Jury‑Duty Call Scheme
Press Release Georgia Inmates Sentenced in Police‑Impersonation Jury‑Duty Call Scheme Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Georgia Inmates Posed as Police, Threatening Citizens and Collecting Payments from Prison ALBANY, Ga. – Two Georgia inmates who orchestrated a phone scheme from behind bars, extorting at least 119 citizens by demanding payment for supposed missed jury‑duty fines, have been sentenced to federal prison following an investigation conducted by the FBI. Lance Riddle, aka “C-Port,” was sentenced to serve a total of 200 months in prison, followed by three years of supervised release, to run consecutively to any state sentence. Co-defendant Joey Amour Jackson, aka “Apes---,” was sentenced to serve a total of 120 months in prison, followed by three years of supervised release, to run consecutively to any state sentence. The Court will determine restitution for both defendants in 90 days. Senior U.S. District Judge W. Louis Sands presided over the sentencing hearings on October 14. Jackson and Riddle were found guilty of one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering on January 9, after a five-day trial that began on January 5. There is no parole in the federal system. “Even from prison, the defendants preyed on citizens through threats and deceit, scams that too many Americans are confronted with today,” said U.S. Attorney William R. ‘Will’ Keyes. “Our office and our law enforcement partners remain firmly committed to protecting the public and ensuring that those who commit fraud face full accountability.” “Not even prison cells prevented these criminals from harming dozens of innocent people. Hopefully, this sentence will bring some level of comfort to the victims and prevent others from falling for similar scams,” said Marlo Graham, Special Agent in Charge of FBI Atlanta. “The FBI will continue to work with our law enforcement partners in not only addressing these types of inmate-based crimes but also in preventing inmates’ access to contraband cell phones that provide the means to do so much harm to the unsuspecting public.” According to court documents and statements referenced at trial, FBI agents in Columbus, Georgia, received information from law enforcement agencies across the U.S. about wire fraud by Georgia inmates, including local law enforcement in Colorado, Florida, Virginia, Nevada, California, and Ohio. Agents discovered that inmates at Calhoun State Prison, including Jackson and Riddle, were using contraband cellular telephones and advanced electronic techniques such as Voice Over Internet Protocol (VOIP) to contact victims from a number that mirrored the numbers of their local police departments. Press Release Justice Department Reaches Settlement Agreement with City of Lexington, Mississippi, Regarding Lexington Police Department’s Unlawful Police Practices Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs The Justice Department announced today that it has obtained an out-of-court settlement agreement with the City of Lexington, Mississippi, to remedy certain violations described in the Department’s Sept. 26, 2024, findings report. Specifically, the Department found that the Lexington Police Department (LPD) engages in a pattern or practice of civil rights violations. “The Department of Justice supports local law enforcement” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights division. “We are very pleased that the City of Lexington and the Lexington Police Department reached an agreement to enhance the lawful and essential activities of the police department and its officers as they continue to protect and serve the citizens of Lexington and its surrounding areas.” “Today’s agreement reflects a shared commitment to meaningful and sustainable change” said U.S. Attorney J.E. Baxter Kruger for the Southern District of Mississippi. “Through these reforms, we seek not only to address the concerns identified in our investigation, but also to strengthen public trust and promote practices that respect the rights and dignity of every person.” As part of the agreement, the City and LPD will amend policies and practices regarding fines and fees, bail and release criteria, and potential conflict of interests. LPD will also revise its policies and practices regarding stops, searches, arrests, and use of force policies and update its reporting and review of such activities by officers. The Department looks forward to working cooperatively with the City and LPD to ensure that they remedy the alleged violations. The Civil Rights Division’s Special Litigation Section and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Mississippi initiated the investigation in March 2023 under 34 U.S.C. 12601 which authorizes the Department to take action to remedy a pattern or practice of deprivation of constitutional rights by state or local law enforcement agencies. Additional information about the Civil Rights Division’s work regarding the conduct of law enforcement agencies is available on its website at: www.justice.gov/crt/conduct-law-enforcement-agencies . title: Oahu Girls’ Wrestling Coach Indicted for Production, Distribution, Receipt, and Possession of Child Pornography and Child Sex Trafficking
text:
Oahu Girls’ Wrestling Coach Indicted for Production, Distribution, Receipt, and Possession of Child Pornography and Child Sex Trafficking
Press Release Oahu Girls’ Wrestling Coach Indicted for Production, Distribution, Receipt, and Possession of Child Pornography and Child Sex Trafficking Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Hawaii HONOLULU – United States Attorney Ken Sorenson announced that Sean Sakaida, 44, of Honolulu, Hawaii, was indicted on October 15, 2026, and charged with four counts of production of child pornography, four counts of distribution of child pornography, one count of receipt of child pornography, four counts of possession of child pornography, and one count of child sex trafficking.  He was previously arrested and taken into custody on September 24, 2026, after being charged by criminal complaint. According to court records, Sakaida, a former coach of the girls’ wrestling team at Moanalua High School, frequently communicated with a minor victim using the messaging application WhatsApp between 2025 and 2026.  In these communications, Sakaida received multiple sexually explicit photographs of the minor victim.  As charged in the indictment, he also produced and distributed multiple videos of himself engaged in sexual acts with the minor victim.  Sakaida was also charged with enticing a second minor victim into engaging in a commercial sex act. If convicted, Sakaida faces at least 15 years and up to 30 years in prison on each production count, at least 5 years and up to 20 years in prison on each distribution and receipt count, up to 10 years in prison on each possession count, up to life in prison on the sex trafficking count, a fine of up to $250,000, plus a term of supervised release. The charges in the indictment are merely accusations, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.  In the case of conviction, any sentence would be imposed by a United States District Judge based on the statutory sentencing factors and the advisory United States Sentencing Guidelines. The FBI is investigating the case. Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Heidi Turner is prosecuting the case. The FBI’s Honolulu Field Office is seeking to identify potential victims of Sean Sakaida. title: New York Man Sentenced to Five Years in Prison for Participating in a Nationwide Bank Fraud Conspiracy
text:
New York Man Sentenced to Five Years in Prison for Participating in a Nationwide Bank Fraud Conspiracy
Press Release New York Man Sentenced to Five Years in Prison for Participating in a Nationwide Bank Fraud Conspiracy Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Alabama MOBILE, AL – A New York man was sentenced to 60 months in prison for participating in a nationwide bank fraud conspiracy involving stolen and counterfeited financial instruments. According to court documents, Curtis Jackson, 31, of Staten Island, New York, admitted that, between February 2023 and June 2024, he conspired with LaEric Marques Williams-Beverly and other conspirators based in Mobile, Alabama, to commit mail theft and bank fraud involving stolen and counterfeited checks. The checks bore the personal identifying information of numerous identity theft victims. Jackson and Williams-Beverly administered an illicit Telegram channel called “House of Pain & Drank,” where millions of dollars’ worth of stolen financial instruments were posted for sale to other fraudsters. In January 2024, agents obtained video footage from a Mobile business (“Business-1”) showing Williams-Beverly stealing checks from the business’s mailbox. Williams-Beverly then coordinated with other coconspirators to counterfeit the checks and fraudulently deposit them into a bank account. ATM surveillance footage captured Williams-Beverly making the fraudulent deposits. Later that month, police in New York City arrested Jackson in possession of a counterfeited check for $43,686.45, drawn on Business-1’s bank account. Jackson had received the check from Williams-Beverly. Jackson’s iCloud account also contained images of stolen and counterfeited checks, including a Citibank deposit slip for a $62,673.46 check drawn on Business-1’s bank account. In June 2024, federal agents executed a search warrant at Williams-Beverly’s home in Mobile. Agents seized numerous pieces of stolen mail, counterfeited checks, debit and credit cards belonging to other individuals, counterfeiting tools, two pistols, and Williams-Beverly’s cell phone. Williams-Beverly admitted to agents that he produced counterfeited checks and coordinated the purchase and sale of stolen checks through the fraudulent Telegram channel he operated with Jackson. Electronic evidence recovered from the conspirators’ cell phones, iCloud accounts, and social media accounts demonstrated the extensive scope of the conspiracy. U.S. District Judge Kristi K. DuBose sentenced Jackson to serve 60 months in federal prison, emphasizing that he was a recidivist with several prior state arrests and convictions for theft, larceny, possession of forged instruments, possession of drugs, and bail jumping. title: Former New Orleans Personal Injury Attorney Sentenced in Connection with Staged Accident Probe
text:
Former New Orleans Personal Injury Attorney Sentenced in Connection with Staged Accident Probe
Press Release Former New Orleans Personal Injury Attorney Sentenced in Connection with Staged Accident Probe Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Louisiana shane.jones@usdoj.gov NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA – DANNY PATRICK KEATING, JR. , age 57, of New Orleans, was sentenced on October 15, 2026 for Conspiracy to Commit Mail and Wire Fraud, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Section 371, arising out of staged automobile accidents with tractor-trailers occurring in New Orleans, announced United States Attorney David I. Courcelle. KEATING was indicted on November 5, 2020, and charged with knowingly engaging in a vast conspiracy involving the intentional staging of motor vehicle collisions with tractor-trailers and commercial vehicles in the metropolitan New Orleans area. Thus far, sixty-three (63) defendants have been charged in the federal probe into the staging of such collisions. KEATING was a personal injury attorney licensed to practice law in Louisiana. At the time of his plea on June 17, 2021, KEATING admitted he knowingly paid Damian Labeaud for thirty-one (31) illegally staged tractor-trailer accidents. KEATING represented seventy-seven (77) plaintiffs involved in the thirty-one (31) accidents staged by Labeaud. KEATING settled seventeen (17) of the thirty-one (31) staged accidents. The indictment charged that KEATING and his clients received a total of approximately $1,500,000.00 in settlement monies resulting from his representation of these clients, and that KEATING kept approximately $358,000.00 of these monies as his attorney’s fees. KEATING admitted filing lawsuits in state and federal court in Louisiana, on behalf of his clients who were involved in the staged accidents. The lawsuits he filed on behalf of the seventy-seven (77) plaintiffs fraudulently misrepresented the identity of the driver of these vehicles, fraudulently misrepresented who was at fault in the staged accidents, and fraudulently claimed injuries. KEATING used the U.S Postal Service to mail settlement demands on behalf of his clients from the Eastern District of Louisiana to various out-of-state locations. In many cases, KEATING ’s clients provided false testimony in depositions taken in conjunction with lawsuits filed by KEATING . United States District Judge Nanette Jolivette Brown sentenced KEATING to thirty-two (32) months of imprisonment, followed by three (3) years of supervised release, as well as the payment of $657,405.34 in restitution, and a $100.00 mandatory special assessment fee. The U.S. Attorney’s Office would like to acknowledge the assistance of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Louisiana State Police, and the Metropolitan Crime Commission with this matter. title: Milwaukee Man Sentenced to 38 Years in Federal Prison for  Murder of Letter Carrier
text:
Milwaukee Man Sentenced to 38 Years in Federal Prison for  Murder of Letter Carrier
Press Release Milwaukee Man Sentenced to 38 Years in Federal Prison for  Murder of Letter Carrier Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Wisconsin Brad D. Schimel, First Assistant United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Wisconsin, announced that on October 14, 2026, United States District Court Chief Judge Pamela Pepper sentenced Kevin McCaa (age 40) of Milwaukee, Wisconsin, to 38 years’ imprisonment, followed by five years of supervised release. On July 8, 2026, Kevin McCaa pled guilty to the murder of a United States Postal Employee and discharge of a firearm during a crime of violence. As detailed in the court record, veteran United States Postal Service letter carrier Aundre Cross was delivering mail in Milwaukee on the afternoon of December 9, 2022, when he was shot in the head and killed. Evidence established that Kevin McCaa and Charles Ducksworth Jr. were responsible for the homicide. McCaa and Ducksworth surveilled the letter carrier for over 30 minutes prior to the homicide and targeted him because they thought he had stolen their drug package. After the homicide, they threw the firearm in a nearby creek, changed their phone numbers, and disposed of clothing.  McCaa and Ducksworth have been in federal custody since their arrest for these offenses on December 27, 2022. At the sentencing hearing, Judge Pepper credited the “old-fashioned” investigative work that led to the arrest of McCaa and Ducksworth. Law enforcement utilized warrants for phone record data, automated license plate reader technology and surveillance footage from numerous residences and businesses in the area of the homicide to show the suspects’ activities before and after the homicide. Judge Pepper further determined that the facts of the case reflected that the crime was “premeditated, planned beforehand, with malice aforethought” and called it “incomprehensible.” “As the Chief Judge noted, these defendants were brought to justice through excellent work by investigators and prosecutors,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Schimel. “This was a cold-blooded, senseless murder of a beloved member of his family and the community he served. McCaa will rightly spend virtually the rest of his life in federal prison.” “Holding those accountable who commit violence against employees of the U.S. Postal Service is our agency’s number one priority. Today’s sentencing hopefully brings a small amount of justice and closure for the family and friends of Aundre Cross. The U.S. Postal Inspection Service would like to thank the Milwaukee Police Department and FBI Milwaukee for their unwavering assistance with this investigation.” stated Nicholas Bucciarelli, Inspector in Charge, Chicago Division of U.S. Postal Inspection Service. “Kevin McCaa’s heinous crime was deserving of the significant sentenc

title: Scotland County Man Convicted on Drug and Firearm Charges
text:
Scotland County Man Convicted on Drug and Firearm Charges
Press Release Scotland County Man Convicted on Drug and Firearm Charges Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of North Carolina GREENSBORO, N.C. – A jury in federal district court convicted VERNON SCOTT NORTON today of multiple drug and firearm charges, announced United States Attorney Dan Bishop of the Middle District of North Carolina. According to court documents, NORTON, age 34, was initially indicted on October 27, 2025, charged in Count One with conspiracy to distribute 500 grams or more of a mixture and substance containing a detectable amount of methamphetamine; in Count Two with possession of a firearm in furtherance of the offense charged in Count One; in Count Three with possession of a machinegun; and in Counts Four and Five with felon in possession of firearms. Evidence at trial showed that NORTON was a previously convicted felon who possessed 31 firearms and a significant quantity of methamphetamine at his trailer in Laurel Hill, North Carolina. On December 29, 2023, law enforcement officers executed a search warrant at the property early in the morning. Officers located eight firearms inside the trailer and 23 additional firearms in a 2005 Infiniti parked in the yard. One of the firearms in the Infiniti was a machinegun—a Glock Model 19X 9mm pistol equipped with a machinegun conversion device. Inside the trailer, officers recovered nearly 1.4 kilograms of methamphetamine hydrochloride. At the time of his arrest, NORTON had more than $6,000 in cash on his person. A readily accessible firearm—a Sturm/Ruger & Co. Inc. Model Ruger P94 9mm pistol—was found resting on the arm of a sofa next to a loaded magazine. Before executing the warrant, law enforcement had conducted multiple controlled purchases of narcotics from the property. A jury convicted NORTON on all counts of the Indictment after a four-day trial. At sentencing, NORTON faces a term of imprisonment of 15 years to life, not less than 5 years of supervised release, fines, and restitution. Sentencing is scheduled for February 17, 2027, before Senior United States District Judge William L. Osteen, Jr. in Greensboro. The case was investigated by the Scotland County Sheriff’s Office and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Frank J. Chut and Chase Stevens. ### Updated October 16, 2026 Component USAO - North Carolina, Middle

title: Evansville Tax Preparer Lands in Federal Prison for $965,000 COVID 19 Tax Credit Fraud
text:
Evansville Tax Preparer Lands in Federal Prison for $965,000 COVID 19 Tax Credit Fraud
Press Release Evansville Tax Preparer Lands in Federal Prison for $965,000 COVID 19 Tax Credit Fraud Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Indiana EVANSVILLE- Tonda Avery, 55, of Evansville, has been sentenced to one year and one day in federal prison, followed by one year of supervised release, after pleading guilty to five counts of Aiding and Assisting in the Preparation and Presentation of a False and Fraudulent Tax Return. Avery was also ordered to pay $1,318,455.43 in restitution. This case was brought as part of the Trump Administration’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud. According to court documents, Avery operated Diversity Tax Service (DTS) in Evansville, Indiana. Avery prepared federal income tax returns for clients and employed other tax return preparers at DTS. Between 2020 and 2021, Avery prepared and filed approximately 123 tax returns containing false Forms 7202, causing a total tax loss of $965,203. Form 7202 allowed eligible self-employed individuals to claim refundable tax credits for certain periods in which they were unable to work because of circumstances related to COVID-19. As part of her scheme, Avery manufactured or inflated her clients’ eligibility for these credits. For clients who did not own legitimate businesses, Avery created fictitious businesses and prepared false Schedule C forms reporting nonexistent business income and expenses. She then used the fictitious businesses to support fraudulent Forms 7202 and claim COVID-19 sick and family leave tax credits to which the clients were not entitled. For clients who did have legitimate businesses, Avery inflated information used to calculate the credits, including the number of days the clients purportedly were unable to work and their net earnings from self-employment. These false figures resulted in the clients claiming larger tax credits and receiving refunds greater than they were entitled to receive. The prevalence of Forms 7202 in Avery’s returns was dramatically higher than among taxpayers generally. In 2020, approximately 33.82% of the returns Avery filed included a Form 7202, compared with approximately 0.90% of returns nationwide and 0.50% of returns in Indiana. In 2021, Forms 7202 appeared on approximately 61.14% of Avery’s returns, compared with approximately 0.90% nationwide and 0.40% in Indiana. Avery also instructed and encouraged other tax return preparers at DTS to prepare fraudulent returns, including returns containing false Forms 7202. Avery charged fees based on the number of forms and schedules included in a tax return. When Avery added a fraudulent Schedule C and Form 7202 to a client’s return, she increased her fee by $800. “Ms. Avery’s scheme exploited pandemic relief programs designed to help Americans in genuine need,” said Tom Wheeler, United States Attorney fo

title: 11th Circuit Affirms Conviction, 30-Year Sentence in Cold Case Prosecution of 2001 Murder of Pregnant Army Private in Germany
text:
11th Circuit Affirms Conviction, 30-Year Sentence in Cold Case Prosecution of 2001 Murder of Pregnant Army Private in Germany
Press Release 11th Circuit Affirms Conviction, 30-Year Sentence in Cold Case Prosecution of 2001 Murder of Pregnant Army Private in Germany Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Pensacola, Florida – The United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit affirmed the conviction and sentence of Shannon L. Wilkerson, 46, for the 2001 murder of 19-year-old Army Private First Class Amanda Gonzales and her unborn child. In May 2024, a Pensacola jury convicted Wilkerson, a former U.S. solider, of second-degree murder. According to court documents, Wilkerson beat and strangled Gonzales to death on November 3, 2001, in her barracks room at Fliegerhorst Kaserne, then a U.S. Army base in Hanau, Germany. Evidence introduced at trial indicated that Wilkerson feared he was the father of Gonzales’ unborn child and that her pregnancy would interfere with his military career and his marriage to another soldier on the base. Wilkerson was a member of the U.S. Armed Forces at the time of the offense but was later discharged. The district court sentenced Wilkerson to 30 years’ imprisonment. United States Attorney John P. Heekin said: “This cold case prosecution demonstrated the lengths to which my office will go to achieve justice for crime victims.  I am extremely proud that we successfully defended this conviction and sentence against the defendant’s appeal. Nothing can bring back the innocent lives taken by this defendant’s heinous crime, but defending this successful prosecution against his appeal ensures he will not escape accountability.” “This case serves as a perfect example of the Criminal Division’s pursuit of justice no matter the challenge,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division.  “I am proud of the work of the Criminal Division prosecutors, the Northern District of Florida, and the federal agents that worked tirelessly to solve this terrible cold case murder.  I also want to express my deepest condolences to the family of PFC Amanda Gonzales and hope that the affirming of Shannon Wilkerson’s conviction by the Court of Appeals brings some sense of closure to this two-decade pursuit of justice.” Following his conviction and sentencing, Wilkerson appealed to the Eleventh Circuit. After briefing by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida defending the conviction and sentence, the Court rejected each of Wilkerson’s arguments in an unpublished opinion without oral argument. title: Previously Convicted Bank Robber Charged Again for Robbing Banks  Wearing “Old Man” Mask
text:
Previously Convicted Bank Robber Charged Again for Robbing Banks  Wearing “Old Man” Mask
Press Release Previously Convicted Bank Robber Charged Again for Robbing Banks  Wearing “Old Man” Mask Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Tampa, Florida – David Sartin, Jr. (40, St. Petersburg) has been charged by criminal complaint with two counts of bank robbery. If convicted, he faces up to 20 years in federal prison on each count. United States Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to court documents, on August 24, 2026, Sartin robbed a bank in Largo. On September 15, 2026, he robbed a bank in St. Petersburg. During both robberies, Sartin entered the bank wearing a prosthetic “old man” mask, approached the teller counter and demanded money, and instructed the teller not to include dye packs. The investigation revealed that Sartin had arrived at a nearby gas station shortly before the first robbery, then drove through the surrounding area before parking, switching to a bicycle, and approaching the bank. After the robbery, Sartin fled on the bicycle, retrieved the staged vehicle, and drove away. The vehicle was later seen on multiple nearby roadways heading in the direction of his residence. Video surveillance captured a vehicle leaving Sartin’s home before the second robbery and returning afterwards. When the vehicle returned to the residence, a white male resembling Sartin was seen unloading a bicycle from the vehicle and rolling it toward the residence. The next day, investigators observed Sartin spray paint the vehicle’s white roof black, making the entire vehicle appear black in color. A search of Sartin’s residence uncovered a bicycle, a blue suit, and a black bag, all similar to the items used during the first robbery. A black suit similar to the one used during the second robbery was also recovered. Investigators also seized materials covered in black spray paint and a receipt for clothing purchased the day before the second robbery. A search of Sartin’s storage unit revealed a backpack and laptop bag containing disguise items matching those seen in the surveillance footage from the robberies, including the old‑man mask with grey facial hair, dark‑framed glasses, and work gloves with black paint on them. The bags also contained a fake handgun and clothing consistent with the disguise worn during the second robbery, including a white dress shirt with black studs, a pinstriped sports coat, a dark blue flat cap, and black dress shoes and pants. Agents also searched another residence where Sartin occasionally stayed. There, they found several items, including a prosthetic mask different from the one used in the robberies and a journal titled, “God’s Best friend is a Bank Robber! Uncle Henry Cops and Robbers the world through the eyes of a Bank Robber.” The journal was dated “Jan 1, 2021,” and was “written by: David Sartin.” O

title: Miracle-Ear and its Foundation Agree to Pay over $6.4 Million to Resolve False Claims Allegations Concerning the Paycheck Protection Program
text:

Press Release Miracle-Ear and its Foundation Agree to Pay over $6.4 Million to Resolve False Claims Allegations Concerning the Paycheck Protection Program Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Wisconsin Brad D. Schimel, First Assistant United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Wisconsin, announced a settlement with Miracle-Ear, Inc., and the Miracle-Ear Foundation to settle claims that they improperly obtained three loans through the Paycheck Protection Program (“PPP”).  Miracle-Ear and its foundation agreed to pay $6,473,222 to resolve the government’s claims. Congress enacted the PPP in March 2020 to provide emergency assistance to small businesses suffering from the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. The program was operated by the Small Business Administration (SBA) and allowed eligible small businesses and nonprofits to receive loans guaranteed by the federal government.  If the borrower spent the funds on qualified expenses, the government repaid the loan on the borrower’s behalf.  To qualify as a small business eligible for a PPP loan, a borrower and any affiliated companies generally could not employ more than 500 individuals.  In its loan application, moreover, the borrower was required to certify that it was eligible for the PPP and that the information provided in the application was accurate. Miracle-Ear distributes and sells hearing aids and associated products through stores owned by Miracle-Ear as well as stores owned and operated by franchisees.  Miracle-Ear Foundation is a nonprofit organization that provides free hearing aids to low-income individuals.  Miracle-Ear received a first-draw PPP loan in the amount of $1,962,000 in June 2020 and a second-draw PPP loan in the amount of $1,962,000 in February 2021. Miracle-Ear Foundation received a single PPP loan in the amount of $58,100 in May 2020. Miracle-Ear is wholly owned by Amplifon (USA) Inc., which, in turn, is wholly owned by Amplifon S.p.A., an Italian public company with thousands of employees and annual sales exceeding 1.5 billion euros in 2020 and 2021. Miracle-Ear Foundation is likewise affiliated with Amplifon S.p.A.  The government alleges that Miracle-Ear and its foundation falsely certified that they were eligible for the PPP loans.  Specifically, the United States alleges that Miracle-Ear and its foundation were not eligible for their PPP loans because they were affiliated with Amplifon S.p.A. and that the Amplifon corporate group employed too many individuals for Miracle-Ear and its foundation to qualify for PPP loans.  The United States further contends that Miracle-Ear provided false information in its loan applications to make it appear that Miracle-Ear was covered by an exemption to the SBA’s affiliation rules

text:
U.S. Attorney’s Office Announces Election Integrity Plan for 2026 General Election and Early Voting in Nevada
Press Release U.S. Attorney’s Office Announces Election Integrity Plan for 2026 General Election and Early Voting in Nevada Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nevada LAS VEGAS – The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Nevada , in coordination with the Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division , announced its comprehensive strategy today to oversee federal voting protections and investigate potential election fraud as early voting begins in Nevada for the 2026 midterm elections . The initiative is part of a nationwide effort to ensure a secure, transparent, and accessible voting process. The U.S. Attorney’s Office, alongside federal law enforcement partners, is prepared to enforce federal election laws vigorously while protecting the right of every legal voter to cast their ballot without intimidation or interference. Voters can consult official Department of Justice and state portals to review federal election laws and eligibility requirements. “Maintaining public confidence in our democratic institutions is a top priority. As Nevadans head to the polls for early voting and utilize the state's mail-in ballot options, our office will work hand-in-hand with federal, state, and local partners to safeguard the integrity of the vote. We are committed to a fair election process where every legal ballot is counted accurately. Every single fraudulent, duplicate, or unlawful ballot cast completely cancels out the vote of an honest citizen. Protecting election integrity isn't about keeping people out; it’s about making sure every legal vote counts,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. Key Enforcement Priorities for the 2026 Election: Protecting Voter Rights: Ensuring that all eligible voters can participate in early voting, mail-in voting, and Election Day voting free from discrimination, harassment, or unlawful coercion. Voter Eligibility and Enforcement: Monitoring compliance with federal laws regarding voter registration and eligibility. For detailed information on ongoing reviews, eligibility laws, or federal penalties, please consult official Department of Justice guidelines and state election authority resources. Combating Election Fraud: Investigating actionable allegations of ballot harvesting, voter impersonation, or intentional disruption of polling places and mail-in ballot processing. Mail-In and Early Voting in Nevada Nevada state election officials have confirmed that early in-person voting and mail-in voting will proceed as scheduled under standard state protocols. Federal oversight will remain active throughout the early voting period to monitor for compliance with the Voting Rights Act and ensure that secure ballot drop boxes and polling locations are unhindered.
